clue.text: Publication, one for long-distance travellers

parts.note: a magazine is a publication, shortened to mag
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A magazine aimed at people who travel great distances.
explanation.definitionFit: The three wise men of the Nativity story journeyed far from the East following a star.

clue.text: Bribes added to exploit weaklings

indicators.note: added to says the bribes come after the exploit word

parts.note: to milk is to exploit
a sop is something given to pacify or bribe

explanation.surface: Extra bribes are used to take advantage of feeble people.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble, timid men are called by this old insult for someone soft as bread soaked in milk.

clue.text: Train delay held up daughter going to dance

indicators.note: held up in a down clue says the pieces read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to rail is to travel by train
a lag is a delay

explanation.surface: A train delay stopped a daughter getting to a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' turns RAIL and LAG together, giving GALLIAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Renaissance court dance in triple time.

clue.text: Partner's bonus initially restricted by impasse on board

indicators.note: restricted by says the first piece is held within the impasse word

parts.note: a deadlock in a game of chess, played on a board, is stalemate

indicators.note: initially points to just the opening letter of the word bonus

explanation.surface: A colleague's extra payment is held up by a deadlock in the boardroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a company board; it means a chessboard. B goes inside STALEMATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A companion from the same stable or organisation is a fellow member or colleague.

clue.text: Trunk springing from tangled roots

indicators.note: tangled says the letters of the word roots are mixed up

explanation.surface: A tree trunk rises from a mass of knotted roots.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Male beast manoeuvred into lead, perhaps

indicators.note: manoeuvred says the letters of male beast are moved about

explanation.surface: A bull is steered into the front position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' reads as the leading position; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is an example of a common, non-precious metal.

clue.text: Get in with force taking bold initiative

parts.note: to get in is to enter
prising is opening with force, as with a lever

explanation.surface: Breaking in forcibly shows real nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone resourceful and daring in starting new ventures shows these qualities.

clue.text: Means business

explanation.surface: A firm's resources, put tersely.
explanation.definitionFit: Agency is the means by which something is done; an agency is also a business providing a service.

clue.text: Make certain to use stick when head's away

indicators.note: when head's away says the first letter of the stick word is dropped

parts.note: to take stick is to receive censure, harsh criticism

explanation.surface: Be sure to scold people while the boss is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to use' is linking padding: the definition is followed by how the wordplay works. CENSURE loses C.
explanation.definitionFit: To guarantee or secure that something happens is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Learner coming to see old master

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British car
a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is one

explanation.surface: A student comes to visit a great painter of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Peter LELY was a 17th-century court portrait painter; Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An old master is a distinguished painter from before about 1800, as this Restoration portraitist was.

clue.text: Put out wood to make attachments to mast

parts.note: someone put out is annoyed, or cross
a wood is made of trees

explanation.surface: Discard timber to make fittings for a ship's mast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as an instruction to discard; it means annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: These are horizontal spars fixed to a mast to spread the rigging, a nautical term.

clue.text: A boy's warning about commotion in treasure house

indicators.note: about says the boy's word goes round the commotion

parts.note: a lad is a boy, and the possessive gives the S
din is a loud commotion
cave, Latin for beware, was the British schoolboy's warning cry

explanation.surface: A boy shouts a warning about the noise in a place full of riches.
explanation.definitionFit: The cave of the Arabian Nights tale is proverbial for a place stuffed with treasure.

clue.text: Housekeeper's store not full yet

parts.note: still and yet are synonyms in 'still to come'
a place not full still has room

explanation.surface: The housekeeper's cupboard isn't stocked up yet.
explanation.definitionFit: In a large house this was the pantry where preserves, cordials and cakes were kept under the housekeeper's charge.

clue.text: New money in sovereigns — come again?

indicators.note: in says the money is placed inside the sovereigns

parts.note: R for rex is a sovereign, and two of them give RR
the ecu was the newly devised European currency unit

explanation.surface: New currency replacing gold sovereigns — will they come back?
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereigns' looks like gold coins but stands for two kings, R + R (rex).
explanation.definitionFit: To happen again or repeat is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Monarch arriving not spotted outside, maybe

indicators.note: outside says the pure word is wrapped round the other pieces

parts.note: something unspotted is pure, without stain
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
an advent is an arrival

explanation.surface: The king turns up, though nobody notices, possibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not spotted' suggests unseen; here it means unblemished.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning perhaps or by chance.

clue.text: Magical performer's energy with new piece on bagpipes

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics
the chanter is the pipe on bagpipes that plays the melody

explanation.surface: A magician's energy is renewed by a new part fitted to the pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorcerer or wizard who casts spells is a magical performer; the 's is read as 'is'.

clue.text: Column's smear about individual

indicators.note: about says the smear word goes round the individual

parts.note: to plaster is to smear thickly
I, the Roman one, stands for an individual

explanation.surface: A newspaper column's slander about one person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Column' suggests a newspaper; it is architectural. I goes inside PLASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangular column set into a wall is this architectural feature; the 's is read as 'is'.

clue.text: SHAPE or other military HQ

explanation.surface: NATO's European headquarters or another army command.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAPE is NATO's Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe, so 'other military HQ' points to the US defence headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-sided figure is a geometric shape, and the five-sided building in Arlington houses the US Department of Defense.

clue.text: President's lease could be a handicap in England

parts.note: Abraham Lincoln was a US president, and the possessive gives the S
to lease is to hire

explanation.surface: An American president's rental agreement might hamper him.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lincolnshire Handicap is a flat horse race run in England; LINCOLNSHIRE is also an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: This English horse race, run at the start of the flat season, is a handicap event named after the county.

clue.text: Associated a line with foreign song

parts.note: lied is the German word for song

explanation.surface: Linked a line of verse with a German song.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined in alliance or connected are synonyms of associated.

clue.text: Skills of curator, primarily with large collections

indicators.note: primarily picks just the opening letter of the word curator

parts.note: a raft is a large number or collection, as in a raft of measures

explanation.surface: A museum curator's talents, mainly with big holdings.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilled trades or abilities are synonyms of skills.

clue.text: Primate left prayer, on departing

indicators.note: departing says the letters named just before it go away

parts.note: an orison is an old word for a prayer
the word on is the part that leaves

explanation.surface: A primate said a prayer before leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: ORISON loses ON to give ORIS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a slow-moving nocturnal Asian primate with large eyes.

clue.text: Climbing a southern slope to secure objective

indicators.note: to secure says the slope word holds the objective inside it

parts.note: a cant is a slope or tilt
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: Going up a south-facing incline to reach a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising or mounting upward is the literal sense, as of a star climbing in the sky.

clue.text: Stop nearby

explanation.surface: A halt close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut down or end is a synonym of stop; near at hand is a synonym of nearby.

clue.text: Fighting to contain French encroachment

indicators.note: to contain says the fighting phrase is wrapped round the French piece

parts.note: troops fighting are in action

explanation.surface: Combat breaks out to keep the French from intruding.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach or violation of a rule is an infringement on what is allowed.

clue.text: Most agree to take part in such a party

indicators.note: take part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Most people agree to join this kind of celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A men-only party before a wedding, a bachelor party in the US, is named with this word.

clue.text: Remove stuffing from food consumed around end of December

parts.note: a dish is a serving of food

indicators.note: around says the eaten word goes round that letter

parts.note: food consumed has been eaten

indicators.note: end of picks the closing letter of December

explanation.surface: Gutting a turkey that was eaten around the end of December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffing' suggests the Christmas turkey; it means courage. R goes inside EATEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To take the stuffing out of someone is an idiom for making them lose heart and confidence.

clue.text: Household implement that's used for making chips

explanation.surface: A domestic tool that turns out chips.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic appliance for pressing clothes; also the golf club used to play short lofted chip shots.
